DETROIT \(AP\) - The U\.S\. Coast Guard has rescued three adults and a child who became stranded on a small island in the Detroit River during a kayaking trip\.

The man, his wife, a 5-year-old girl, and a family friend became stranded on the island in the river’s mouth Friday after launching their kayaks from Lake Erie Metropark\.

Rescue crews were sent on a boat and a helicopter, but the water around the island proved too shallow for the boat\.

The kayakers were hoisted into the helicopter after 7 p\.m\. and taken to Gross Ile Municipal Airport, and treated for mild hypothermia\.

The Coast Guard says the kayakers spent about four hours stranded, but were prepared with a survival kit and cell phones and had also lit a bonfire to stay warm\.

Copyright © 2026 The Washington Times, LLC\.

MENU

**JACKSON KAYAK AND WERNER PADDLES – STRONGER TOGETHER**

**A new alliance between Jackson Kayak and Werner Paddles signifies a powerful partnership that is built on shared values and a commitment to excellence\. **

Jackson, and Werner are proud to continue a legacy of supporting specialty shops with exclusive products and top-end service\. We are proud to say that specialty shops are the key focus of our sales efforts\.

“We have a strong team, a very large facility, and our location is ideal for growth,” says Peter Hausin, CEO of Jackson Kayak, now the parent company of both brands\. “We knew that we would be stronger if we were a larger company, so we are thrilled to now be joining forces with Werner, one of the premier brands in paddlesports\.”

A meeting between Bruce Furrer, longtime owner of Werner Paddles, and Tony Lunt, co-founder and majority owner of Jackson Kayak, solidified the alignment of business values and reinforced the shared dedication to paddling, employee and community support, and delivering quality products\. “After meeting with Tony, I quickly learned of his long-term involvement in paddlesports, his belief in supporting employees, and his commitment to producing the highest quality products,” says Furrer\. “I’m comfortable Werner Paddles is in good hands\.”

Moving forward, both companies’ Sales and Marketing teams will continue to operate independently, remaining committed to delivering the highest quality services to their customers\. Paddle production will transition to the Jackson location in Sparta, TN\. “We know that it is critical to preserve the individuality of each brand,” says Hausin\. “We can be a stronger and more efficient company together, but we will not abandon the uniqueness of these two stellar brands\.”

The alliance between Jackson Kayak and Werner Paddles signals a new chapter in the paddlesports industry, driven by shared values, manufacturing expertise, and a commitment to customer satisfaction\. Together, they stand poised to lead the way in delivering exceptional paddling experiences to enthusiasts worldwide\.

### **About Jackson Kayak**

Jackson Kayak was founded in 2004 and resides in Sparta, Tennessee, with over 100 employees\. Jackson Kayak immediately became a leading whitewater brand and quickly evolved into the recreational and fishing kayak sectors\. Jackson has since expanded their high-end kayak product line to include accessories, including Orion Coolers\. These initiatives have helped Jackson Kayak reach more and more outdoor enthusiasts worldwide\. Jackson Kayak remains a family-owned and operated company today and continues to be a made-in-the-USA manufacturer, supporting Tennessee’s local economy\.  
**For more information, contact Emily Jackson – Marketing Director, at** emily@jacksonkayak\.com

### **About Werner Paddles**

Werner Paddles began with Werner and Martha Furrer’s first kayaking adventure together in 1955\. With limited gear available, Werner Sr built his first kayak in 1959 and subsequently his first paddle in 1965\. With a growing family, each member needed a kayak and paddle, and the Furrer garage became a workshop to deliver the gear\. From that humble beginning grew a company of dedicated craftsmen and women who bring passion, commitment, and pride to work every single day\. Today, Werner Paddles takes an engineering and technological approach to design\. Function, ergonomics, durability, and beauty are key requirements for the best paddling experience\. We take pride in handcrafting products in the U\.S\., minimising waste, taking care of our people, and giving back to the local community\. Whether you spend the day paddling on flat water with your family or rely on your paddle in Class V rapids, we continuously innovate to deliver Ultimate Paddle Performance\.  
**For more information, contact Taylor Robertson – Director of Sales and Marketing at** taylor\.robertson@wernerpaddles\.com

# How Kozhikode’s Malabar River Festival became Asia’s biggest kayaking event - CNBC TV18

## Kozhikode's Malabar River Festival: How a rural Kerala river became Asia's biggest kayaking event

## From a Google Maps search to an internationally recognised sporting event, here's how the Malabar River Festival helped turn Kozhikode into India's white-water kayaking hub while boosting adventure tourism and the local economy\.

A rural stretch of Kozhikode in Kerala has transformed into one of Asia's leading white-water kayaking destinations, thanks to monsoon-fed rapids, strong local support and sustained government backing\.

When Manik Taneja, founder of the Malabar River Festival, first typed \"river rapids\" into Google Maps, he wasn't looking for a holiday spot—he was searching for a place where India could develop white-water kayaking\. What he found on the screen was a rural stretch of Kozhikode\. What he found on the ground was what is now Asia's biggest kayaking festival\.

Kozhikode is once again hosting the Malabar River Festival, now in its 12th edition, bringing together kayakers from across India and abroad for a three-day white-water competition\. Held on the rapids of Thusharagiri's Chalipuzha and Iruvazhinjipuzha rivers, the festival is organised by the Kerala Adventure Tourism Promotion Society \(KATPS\), the District Tourism Promotion Council \(DTPC\) and the Kozhikode District Panchayat, with technical support from the Indian Kayaking and Canoeing Association \(IKCA\)\. The event highlights Kerala's growing reputation as an adventure tourism destination\.

The Kerala government has allocated ₹50 lakh for the event, said Binu Kuriakose, CEO of KATPS\. He added that several pre-events were organised ahead of the festival to build awareness and encourage participation\. The event will be jointly conducted by eight panchayats in Kozhikode district, with the government allocating ₹2 lakh each to the participating grama panchayats\.

Kuriakose said the festival also boosts the local economy, with participants and visitors from across India and abroad spending on homestays, restaurants and small businesses in the region\. He added that the increased footfall creates seasonal employment opportunities while bringing greater visibility to the area\. The event attracts not only kayakers but also spectators, helping promote Kozhikode as an adventure tourism destination\.

One visitor who came to watch the competition said such skills should be taught to more people, especially in a state like Kerala, where heavy monsoon rains frequently lead to floods and other natural disasters\.

**What is white-water kayaking?**

White-water kayaking is a sport in which paddlers navigate kayaks through fast-moving, turbulent rivers, often over rapids and around rocks or other obstacles\. Unlike flat-water kayaking, it requires strong boat control, quick reflexes and the ability to read constantly changing river conditions\.

**The man who put Kerala on the kayaking map**

Manik Taneja, the man behind bringing kayaking to rural Kozhikode, said the Kerala government has supported the sport more consistently than many other states and even the Centre\. He recalled that when the concept first took shape in 2012, the event received just ₹2\.5 lakh in government funding\. That support has since increased to around ₹50 lakh, along with a significantly larger prize pool\.

Taneja said he discovered the site through Google Maps while searching for a suitable river stretch after kayakers in Bengaluru struggled to find proper white-water training rivers\. Unlike many other locations, he said, Kerala's local communities welcomed the idea and the river conditions proved ideal for the sport\.

What began as a small initiative has now developed into a wider ecosystem\. Three kayaking schools now operate in the region during the monsoon season, training aspiring paddlers and helping Kozhikode emerge as a recognised hub for white-water kayaking in India\.

**A global paddler's Kerala experience**

Ryan O'Connor, winner of the Rapid Raja 2025 title, said Kozhikode stood out for its unique setting\. He described the warm rivers and monsoon conditions as \"a super cool environment\" and praised the Kerala Adventure Tourism Promotion Society for promoting the sport internationally\.

He added that stronger support for local paddlers would further strengthen Kerala's kayaking ecosystem and attract more international participants in the coming years\.

**The amateur who stunned the field**

Meanwhile, Muskaan S\. from Karnataka, who won the Amateur Women category after just 20 days of training in white-water kayaking, said the victory came as a surprise\.

\"I was not confident enough before the race as it was my first ever competition and there were kayakers who had more experience than me\. But my team supported me, helped me with the equipment and kept motivating me throughout the race\. Support from my parents also helped me\. I stuck to my strategy and stayed calm throughout,\" she said\.

India's kayaking and canoeing community has grown steadily in recent years, aided by events such as the Malabar River Festival and increased access to training\. With more kayaking schools opening around Kozhikode and more athletes taking up the sport during the monsoon season, the festival has evolved into both a major sporting event and a tourism success story, helping put Kerala on the global white-water kayaking map\.

\(Edited by : Priyanka Deshpande\)

# Kayaker without life-jacket rescued near Petrie Island

Staff Reporter

Updated Wed, August 12, 2026 at 8:25 p\.m\. UTC

1 min read

Ottawa Fire Services rescued a kayaker in the Ottawa River near Petrie Island on Wednesday, Aug\. 12, 2026\. \(Credit: X\)

A kayaker who wasn't wearing a life-jacket was rescued in the Ottawa River near Petrie Island on Wednesday afternoon\.

Ottawa Fire Services said a 911 call at 2:30 p\.m\. reported that the kayaker had flipped off his own watercraft\. After arriving at the location in the city's east end, the OFS water rescue team confirmed the kayaker was hanging on to a friend's kayak and they were both about one kilometre from shore\.

The OFS team launched at the scene and the rescue was completed at 2:47 p\.m\.

Firefighters assessed both individuals and confirmed there were no injuries, an OFS social-media post said\.

It was later confirmed that the two kayakers had unintentionally drifted away from the beach while talking and did not realize how far they had travelled, OFS added\. Waves caused their kayaks to take on water, and one kayaker was eventually unable to remain in their kayak and became stranded in the strong current\.

There was a second water-rescue incident later in the day in the city's west end\.

Ottawa Fire Services said the Ottawa Police Service had reported at 6:35 p\.m\. that a swimmer also without a life-jacket was in distress in the water in the area of Britannia Beach\.

An OFS water-rescue team was again launched at that scene and a rescue was made at 6:57 p\.m\., a news release said\.

# Newlyweds start kayak and canoe rentals at Dover's Nebi Park\. See rates, details\.

DOVER — Newly married couple Maya and Paul Halthore-Kelley are opening Cochecho River Recreation, offering kayak and canoe rentals and a snack bar at the city's new Nebi Park, with a grand opening Saturday, July 25\.

Kayak and canoe rentals will start right away with the snack bar planned to open in the coming weeks when permitting is in place, according to Maya\. Public boat storage will also be offered for New Hampshire and Dover residents to keep their boats near the park's paddle sports dock\. Discounted memberships for Dover residents, students and seniors will be offered\.

Maya said the couple found out in April the city had accepted their proposal to operate the business at the new park, and they got married in May\.

\"It all happened really fast\. It was a really lovely way to kick off our marriage,\" she said\. \"It was like, 'Not only do we get to start our marriage, but we get to start this business together and what a fun adventure it'll be together\.'\"

## What are kayak and canoe rental prices at Nebi Park?

For the first year, Cochecho River Recreation will be open Saturdays and Sundays from 10 a\.m\. to 6 p\.m\. with plans to operate seven days a week next year\. The operating season is May to October\. The end date in 2026 is Oct\. 18\.

Single kayak rates are $30 for up to 90 minutes, $42 for 90 minutes to 3 hours, or $55 for 3-5 hours\.

Canoes and tandem kayaks cost $45 for up to 90 minutes, $60 for 90 minutes to 3 hours, or $75 for 3-5 hours\. A three-visit pass for up to 90 minutes each time costs $90\.

Memberships are also available for individuals or families with various rates\.

For personal boat storage, they currently have one rack built and are working on building out more\. She said they have outdoor storage for kayaks, \"steps away\" from the paddle sports dock\. Maya said kayak owners will have their own lock and key with access whenever the park is open\. She noted they're working on building indoor storage space, too\. The cost is $150 for the season\.

An introduction to kayak clinic will be offered on the first and third Saturdays of each month, Maya said\. She said her husband Paul certified to teach an American Canoe Association accredited kayak clinic\.

\"It just prepares you for boating safety, learning how to paddle, the strokes, understanding the landscapes of water, where you can and can't go, and just kind of gets people, regardless of skill level, comfortable and ready to go out on the water,\" she said\.

## The couple behind Cochecho River Recreation

Maya said Paul is from western Massachusetts and grew up kayaking\. She said his first job was at a boathouse, and he became an environmental educator for Mass Audubon\.

She said his specialty is kayaking, he runs a nature center in Cambridge, and \"loves to do community programs and get people involved and out in nature on the waterfront and specifically kayaking on the water, that's his passion\. He's always dreamed of running a kayak shop himself\.\"

Maya said he started a paddle tour in recent years to an oyster farm in Great Bay operated by friends\. This experience led to the opportunity in Dover\.

\"It was the perfect time because I was working in the restaurant industry, and we were like a kayak rental/snack bar would be awesome for a waterfront space,\" Maya said\. \"We were really excited\.\"

She said after focusing on rentals this summer, next year the couple wants to \"dive deep into community programming, have events for our neighbors\. \" This could include nature programs and summer camps for kids, she said\.
